investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser/JS execution) against the venue's own official '/agenda-concerts/' page, plus two individual event detail pages fetched to check field consistency (time/price/address). The listing page's own JSON-LD is Organization/Breadcrumb metadata only (no Event/MusicEvent node) — the real event data lives in a static WordPress 'portfolio' custom-post-type grid, one card per event, each stating its own date as a 'DD.MM.YY <Title>' prefix in both its <h3> text and its own permalink slug.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of the venue's official '/agenda-concerts/' page immediately exposed 21 real, static, dated event cards (WordPress 'portfolio' custom post type) — each with its own DD.MM.YY-prefixed title, permalink URL, and category (concert/after). No further escalation was needed; Level 1 fully answered the investigation question.

venue_reference: Glazart (live music venue and club), 7-15 Avenue de la Porte de la Villette, 75019 Paris

identity.notes: The retained agenda page's own og:title reads 'AGENDA → GLAZART Paris' at the venue's own self-hosted domain www.glazart.com. The retained event-detail page's own footer widget directly states the full postal address '7/15 Avenue de la Porte de la Villette, 75019 Paris', matching this task's assigned address exactly — a self-consistent, first-party retained artifact.

site_classification.platform: WordPress with a custom 'portfolio' post type (no calendar/events plugin, no JSON-LD Event node — the page's own JSON-LD is All-in-One-SEO's generic Organization/Breadcrumb/WebPage schema only). The agenda page's static HTML directly embeds every currently-listed event as one card each, no pagination observed within the 21 cards retained.

title.notes: Each card's own <h3><a> text states its title directly, immediately following its own 'DD.MM.YY' date prefix (stripped by the collector, not part of the title itself).

start_date.notes: Each card's own <h3><a> title text AND its own permalink URL both state the date as a leading 'DD.MM.YY' (e.g. '15-09-26' / '15.09.26'), a two-digit year. Expanding 'YY' to '20YY' is a direct, literal transcription of exactly what the source states — the same established convention already used in this project for ausland-berlin/admiralspalast-berlin/galeria-ze-dos-bois (see ingestion/admiralspalast/observation-adapter.mjs's own doc comment): this project's live listings only ever run in the 2020s, and the two digits are read exactly as printed, never guessed from today's date. Cross-checked across all 21 sampled cards (29.08.26, 30.08.26, 06.09.26, 15.09.26, 17.09.26, ... all self-consistent between title and permalink slug). One honest caveat: this one sampled event's own free-text BODY copy (a Facebook-style pasted blurb) separately states 'Mardi 17.09.26' near the top before also stating 'Mardi 15 Septembre 2026' further down — an internal inconsistency in the venue's own copy for this one record. The investigation treats the structured <h3>/permalink date (self-consistent, WordPress-generated, matching the site-wide pattern) as authoritative rather than the free-text body blurb, and flags this as a MINOR data-quality risk (see collector_assessment.blockers) rather than downgrading the whole field.

time.notes: Not present on the list page itself. One sampled 'concert'-category detail page states an explicit doors time in free text ('🕒 Ouverture des portes: 19.00'); one sampled 'after'-category detail page states a differently-shaped operating-hours range ('Samedi 29.08.2026 > 06H – 16H') that also appears, unchanged, as this venue's site-wide boilerplate footer note ('After : 6h-16h / 6h-7h Happy Hour !') — i.e. likely generic recurring-series copy, not a per-event-specific time. Format is inconsistent between event types and only reachable per-event (not on the list page), so this bounded collector does not harvest it (matching the admiralspalast-berlin-01 precedent of not fetching every detail page to stay bounded).

end.notes: No reliable, per-event-specific end/close time concept was found. The one number that could be read as an 'end' (the after-party sample's '16H') is the same value as this venue's own site-wide boilerplate footer opening-hours note, not evidence of a genuine per-event value.

venue_location.value: Glazart, 7/15 Avenue de la Porte de la Villette, 75019 Paris
venue_location.notes: The retained event-detail page's own footer widget ('Infos pratiques') states the full address directly; single-venue source, resolved by source_id (venue_name is set to 'Glazart' as an override, matching the LAV/Tempodrom precedent for a single-venue source whose own per-record location field is absent).

source_record_id.notes: No numeric ID is exposed; each event's own WordPress permalink slug (e.g. 'https://www.glazart.com/15-09-26-concert-funebrarum/') is used as source_record_id, the same documented judgement already established for badehaus-berlin/tempodrom-berlin (own URL-slug permalink).

event_url.notes: Each card's own <a href> is this source's own permanent per-event page URL, stated directly.

price.notes: Not present on the list page itself. Both sampled event-detail pages state a price in free text ('🎟️ Tickets: 15€ / 18€ sur place' and 'Sur place avant 12h : 9,50...') — genuinely present per-event, but only reachable by fetching each event's own detail page individually, which this bounded collector does not do (see 'time' above for the same bounding rationale).

blockers.description: One sampled event's own free-text body copy states a conflicting date ('Mardi 17.09.26') alongside its own correct structured date ('15.09.26', matching its own title and permalink slug) — an internal inconsistency in the venue's own page copy, not in this collector's parsing. Does not affect the structured <h3>/permalink date this collector actually relies on, but documents a real data-quality risk on this source.

reasons: Identity PROVEN from a self-consistent retained artifact (page og:title, footer address matching the task's assigned address).

No unresolved CRITICAL blocker — only one honestly-documented MINOR data-quality risk on a single sampled record's free-text body copy, which does not affect the structured fields this collector actually relies on.
